title: Longest Subarray with Equal 0s and 1s
source: Classic prefix-sum + hashing problem (LeetCode 525 'Contiguous Array' family)
statement:
You are given a binary array `A` of length `N` (every element is `0` or `1`).

A **subarray** is a contiguous, non-empty part of the array `A[l..r]`.

Find the **maximum length** of a subarray that contains **the same number of `0`s and `1`s**.

If no such subarray exists, print `0`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `N`.
The second line contains `N` space-separated integers `A[1..N]`, each `0` or `1`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum length of a subarray with equally many `0`s and `1`s, or `0` if there is none.

samples.explanation: The first six elements `0 1 0 0 1 1` contain three `0`s and three `1`s. No subarray of length 7 can be balanced because 7 is odd.
There is no `0` at all, so no balanced subarray exists.

hints: Replace every `0` by `-1`. Then a subarray has equal 0s and 1s exactly when its **sum is 0**.
Let `P[i]` be the prefix sum of the first `i` elements (with `P[0] = 0`). The subarray `A[l+1..r]` has sum 0 exactly when `P[l] == P[r]`.

To maximise `r - l` for equal prefix values, store only the **first** index at which each prefix value appears in a dictionary. Remember to seed it with `{0: -1}` (or `{0: 0}` if you count prefix lengths).
editorial:
### Intuition
Counting zeros and ones separately for every subarray is O(N²). Turn the condition into a **sum**: map `0 → -1`, `1 → +1`. A subarray is balanced ⇔ its sum is `0`.

With prefix sums `P` (`P[0] = 0`, `P[i] = P[i-1] + value[i]`), sum of `A[l+1..r]` = `P[r] - P[l]`. So we need two indices with **equal prefix value**, as far apart as possible.

### Approach
- Walk left to right maintaining the running prefix `pref`.
- Keep a dictionary `first[pref_value] = earliest index where this value occurred`, initialised with `first[0] = -1` (the empty prefix before index 0).
- At index `i`: if `pref` was seen before, candidate length = `i - first[pref]`; otherwise record `first[pref] = i`.
- **Never overwrite** an existing entry — the earliest index gives the longest subarray.

### Complexity
**O(N)** time and **O(N)** extra space (the prefix value is in `[-N, N]`, so an array of size `2N+1` also works).

### Common mistakes
- Forgetting the `{0: -1}` seed — then balanced subarrays that start at index 0 are missed (sample 1).
- Updating `first[pref]` every time (stores the *latest* index → gives shorter answers).
- Using 0/1 directly instead of -1/+1: a prefix-sum difference of 0 would then mean "no ones", not "balanced".
